title: Kapwing vs VEED: caption fixes, team review and dubbing costs
summary: Compare Kapwing and VEED for corrected captions, private review, subtitle files and dubbing. Plan one complete delivery job before buying editor seats or credits.
body_markdown:
Start with VEED when one editor needs to share exported videos with outside reviewers without granting workspace access. Evaluate Kapwing when collaborators need a shared editing workspace and transcript review before dubbing. Both can caption and translate footage. Compare who approves the work, which files you deliver and what each revision consumes.


Magic Hour publishes this comparison and offers a competing creative product. We reviewed official documentation on November 3, 2026. We did not run matched output-quality, transcription-accuracy, speed or cost benchmarks. The tutorial workload and arithmetic are planning examples, not observed invoices or performance results. Confirm current plan access, allowances and checkout terms before buying.


## The decision at a glance


Decision

## Correct the words before styling the captions


Kapwing supports automatic captions, manual entry and imported SRT or VTT files. You can correct text and timing, then reuse subtitle styles through its Brand Kit. That suits a recurring series where product names, fonts and placement should stay consistent across episodes.


VEED documents transcript correction, low-confidence word highlights, a dictionary and timing adjustments. Its guide recommends regenerating subtitles after completing video edits. Treat the cut as a dependency: deleting a sentence after approving the captions can leave a different timing problem from a misspelled name.


Use a representative passage containing an unfamiliar name, a number and a speaker change. Check the actual correction steps and the final line breaks. This is a proposed acceptance check, not a claim that we measured either product’s transcription accuracy.


Sources:[Kapwing caption editing and file workflow](https://www.kapwing.com/help/add-captions/) ·[VEED automatic subtitles and correction](https://support.veed.io/en/articles/11172739-how-to-add-subtitles-to-your-video-automatically)


## A reviewer is not automatically an editor seat


VEED’s Project Viewer role is free and grants access to one exported video, including a private project. It does not open the editor or the rest of the workspace. Workspace Editor invitations may incur charges. This is a useful distinction when a manager only needs to watch a finished version.


Kapwing bills paid workspaces per member. Its current pricing page also allows private-project access for added collaborators, while its older sharing guide describes workspace membership. Confirm the invited role, private access and charge before assuming an outside reviewer needs a paid seat.


For confidential footage, do not make a link public merely to avoid buying a seat. Ask the vendor to confirm the exact permission and billing arrangement your team needs.


Sources:[VEED Project Viewer access and charges](https://support.veed.io/en/articles/10539457-how-to-invite-a-project-viewer) ·[Kapwing sharing and workspace membership](https://www.kapwing.com/help/share-workspace/) ·[Kapwing current private-project and collaborator permissions](https://www.kapwing.com/pricing)


## Specify both the video and the subtitle file


A captioned MP4 and an SRT file are different deliverables. Burned-in captions are part of the picture; a separate timed-text file lets a supported player display captions independently. It does not preserve every animated caption treatment from the editor.


Both vendors describe subtitle-file downloads, but access depends on the plan. Kapwing documents SRT and VTT downloads for Pro. VEED’s subtitle page requires an upgrade for subtitle-file downloads. Confirm this separately from the ability to generate captions or export a video.


If your destination needs bilingual captions, check the displayed result as well as translation availability. VEED’s translation guide says multiple language tracks cannot be shown simultaneously, and its translation workflow cannot translate captions already burned into an uploaded video. Keep the editable transcript.


Sources:[Kapwing subscription and subtitle export FAQ](https://www.kapwing.com/help/subscription-faq/) ·[VEED subtitle downloads](https://www.veed.io/tools/add-subtitles) ·[VEED translated subtitle tracks](https://support.veed.io/en/articles/11508601-how-to-translate-your-subtitles)


## Approve the translation before generating the voice


Kapwing’s dubbing guide offers a review step with source transcription and translation side by side before text-to-speech processing. It also accepts an existing translated SRT or VTT as the basis for a dub. Verify your chosen plan includes the route you need.


VEED’s AI Dubbing guide reserves Proofread and script-file upload for Enterprise. Proofread can validate the translation without deducting dubbing credits, although an adequate balance is required. An uploaded script replaces the spoken source for dubbing: the generated voice follows that file. Review its meaning and timings before proceeding.


This matters for a product demonstration. An approved caption file with the wrong button name should not become the source for six translated voiceovers. Keep a clearly named approved version, and have someone who understands the target language check instructions, numbers and safety statements.


Sources:[Kapwing pre-dub review and translated files](https://www.kapwing.com/help/how-to-dub-on-kapwing/) ·[VEED dubbing and Enterprise proofreading](https://support.veed.io/en/articles/10406623-how-to-use-the-ai-dubbing-tool)


## Worked budget: three tutorials, two languages, two reviewers


Suppose one editor is preparing three two-minute tutorials, each with English captions and Spanish and French versions. Two colleagues must approve the exported videos. This is an illustrative workload, not a reported production test.


The brief contains six source minutes and twelve target-language minutes. Kapwing’s published subtitle rates are one credit per transcription minute and two per translated minute. Those operations alone would total 30 credits: six plus 24. This excludes dubbing, other AI operations, retries and any minimum charges relevant to additional tasks.


VEED’s pricing FAQ counts each translated language against the translation allowance. It separately describes paid subtitle generation with a 50-hour monthly fair-use limit. However, its translation help also refers to AI credits. Confirm how the exact account meters this job rather than treating every allowance as interchangeable.


For this one-editor brief, evaluate VEED first if exported-video viewing is enough for approval. If colleagues must change the timeline together, compare editable-seat costs instead. If dubbing needs approval of an uploaded script, confirm VEED Enterprise access or evaluate Kapwing’s documented pre-dub route before paying.


Leave room for corrections. Kapwing’s dubbing FAQ says transcript changes can consume translation minutes, while regenerating an audio section uses text-to-speech minutes. A completed first pass does not establish that subsequent revisions are free.


Sources:[Kapwing tool credit rates](https://www.kapwing.com/help/subscription-faq/) ·[VEED seats, subtitle fair use and translation allowances](https://www.veed.io/pricing) ·[Kapwing dubbing revision allowances](https://www.kapwing.com/help/dubbing-faqs/)


## Keep the finishing editor when only one shot is missing


A missing visual does not require moving the whole caption project. For a targeted change inside existing footage, Magic Hour AI Video Editor lets you upload a clip and describe the visual edit. Review the current input requirements and credit quote, then return an accepted result to your finishing editor for captions, timing and sound.


Keep the original recording, approved transcript and delivery exports separately. A subscription or watermark-free download does not establish permission to use a person’s voice, likeness, music or third-party footage.
